Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:8: Now, the beginning of subduing the inclination is in the days of youth, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained in the Yalkut (Mishlei, remez 961): "whoever sweetens his inclination in his youth will in the end have it stretched taut over him in his old age. Why? 'He who pampers his servant from youth, his end will be that he becomes a master' [gently paraphrasing Proverbs 29:21]" - and the "servant" is the evil inclination, which is a servant to a person for the needs of this world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:9: One must always be careful of light [sins], for the evil inclination does not trip a person up at first except with light [sins], until from light ones he comes to grave ones - as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Sukkah 52a), on the verse (Isaiah 5:18), "woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of falsehood" - in these words: "Rabbi Yosi said: the evil inclination is at first like a spider's thread, and in the end like cart ropes" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:10: And it is written in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Self-Reckoning, chapter 3, the fourteenth reckoning), in these words: "awaken, my brother, from this sleep, and roll away from your heart the veil poured over you by your inclination, until it has separated between your [inner] light and the light of your intellect - like a spider that weaves over the window of the house, and as it continues, thickens and stops it up until it prevents the sunlight from reaching the house. At the beginning of its weaving it is thin and very weak, but the more it continues, the thicker and stronger it becomes, and it prevents the sunlight from passing through it and reaching the house. So too the working of the inclination in your heart: at the beginning of its matter it is very weak and will not prevent you from seeing the truths; and if you become aware of it at that time and remove it from your heart, the matter will become easy for you; but if you take it lightly and disregard it, its work will strengthen and prevent the light of your intellect from revealing it to your awareness. Therefore, hasten to save your soul, and seek help from God to push it away from you, and labor and exert yourself - you will be illuminated with the light of wisdom and see the truth of matters with the eye of your heart. And our predecessors already compared the working of the inclination in a person to parables drawn from Scripture (II Samuel 12:4), 'and a traveler came to the rich man' - and afterward it calls him 'wayfarer,' and afterward 'man'; and it says (Psalms 1:1), 'happy is the man who has not walked,' and so on, and afterward 'stood,' and afterward 'sat'" - to this point. More on the enticements of the inclination in the next chapter, from a passage of the Zohar - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:11: One must also be careful and examine one's deeds regarding sins that a person tramples underfoot [treats lightly], as our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the Mechilta (see Sifrei, Ha'azinu), and likewise in Avodah Zarah, first chapter (18a): Reish Lakish said, "sins that a person tramples underfoot in this world surround him for the Day of Judgment." And concerning this the daughter of Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon was punished, for Rabbi Yochanan said: once she was walking before the nobles of Rome, and they said, how lovely are the steps of this young woman! She immediately began to take careful note of her steps [becoming self-conscious/vain about them], and they placed her in a brothel. And when she was brought out [innocent, in the account], she justified the judgment upon herself, [citing] "great in counsel," and so on, "whose eyes are open upon all the ways of the sons of man" (Jeremiah 32:19) - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:12: Similarly, it is explained in the Zohar (Miketz 198a): "Rabbi Elazar opened [with the verse] (Psalms 49:6), 'why should I fear in days of evil, when the iniquity of my heels surrounds me?' Come and see: there are three kinds [of fear] - some fear and know what they fear, and this has been established; but there is one who fears and does not know what he fears - such as those sins that he does not know are sins and pays no heed to, and he fears 'days of evil.' What are these 'days of evil'? These are days appointed for that evil. And who is this? The evil inclination, which is called 'evil,' and it has known days when permission is given to it in the world to lead astray all those who defile their ways - for whoever comes to defile himself, they defile him - and these are called 'days of evil,' and these are appointed over those sins that people trample underfoot with their heels.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:13: Come and see: all those who defile their ways - how many bundles of impure spirits are assembled against them and defile them; on the way that a person wishes to walk, they literally lead him," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:14: Come and see: at the time when harsh judgment rules, it does not hold back its hand from doing harm; but at the time when the right rules over the idolatrous nations, to break them, the Holy One, blessed be He, has compassion on them and does not destroy them. And therefore, whoever sins with those sins that he tramples underfoot and does not know of them - he is always in fear. King David was always careful of these sins, and when he went out to war he would examine himself for them, and therefore he did not fear to wage war against them. And come and see - there were four kings [in the account]: whoever asked of this did not ask of that, and so on. Therefore a person must guard himself from these sins, as has been said, so that these 'days of evil,' which show no mercy on him, should not rule over him" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:15: Regarding something similar, the Torah commanded concerning the priest anointed for war, who was to speak to the people and say (Deuteronomy 20:8), "who is the man who is fearful and fainthearted" - and it is explained (Sotah, chapter 8, mishnah 5) that this refers to one who is fearful because of the transgressions in his hand. And our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Menachot 36a) that one who converses between the tefillin of the hand and the tefillin of the head must return from the ranks of battle.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:16: Further, our Sages, of blessed memory, said in Bava Kamma, chapter "Shor SheNagach" (50a): "whoever says the Holy One, blessed be He, is lenient [foregoes strict justice] - his life will be foregone [forfeited]," as it is said (Deuteronomy 32:4), "the Rock, His work is perfect, for all His ways are justice." And further there, in these words: "(Psalms 50:3), 'and round about Him it storms greatly' - this teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, is exacting with His pious ones even to a hairsbreadth. Rabbi Chanina said, from here (ibid. 89:8), 'a God greatly dreaded in the assembly of the holy ones, and awesome above all who are around Him.'"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:17: Further, it is said in Bereshit Rabbah (19:1), on "for with much wisdom comes much vexation, and he who increases knowledge increases pain" (Ecclesiastes 1:18): "from here, when a person increases wisdom upon himself, he increases vexation upon himself, and when he increases knowledge, he increases pain," and so on. Rav said, a scholar needs no warning [before punishment]. Rabbi Yochanan said, like fine linen garments that come from Beit Shean - if they become slightly scorched they are ruined, but linen garments from Arbel, however scorched, retain their value. It was taught in the name of Rabbi Meir: according to the greatness of the serpent was its downfall - "more cunning than all" [became] "more cursed than all" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:18: One must also fear and be careful in his deeds, for perhaps he and the world are half meritorious and half guilty, and he tips the balance for himself and for the whole world to the side of guilt. And so our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Kiddushin 40b): "our Rabbis taught: a person should always view himself as though he were half meritorious and half guilty. If he performs one commandment, happy is he, for he has tipped the balance for himself to the side of merit; if he commits one transgression, woe to him, for he has tipped the balance for himself to the side of guilt, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 9:18), 'and one sinner destroys much good' - because of a single sin that this one committed, much good was lost to him. Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says: since the world is judged according to its majority, and the individual is judged according to his majority - if he performs one commandment, happy is he, for he has tipped the balance for himself and for the whole world to the side of merit; if he commits one transgression, woe to him, for he has tipped the balance for himself and for the whole world to the side of guilt, as it is said, 'and one sinner destroys much good' - because of a single sin that this one committed, much good was lost from him and from the world" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:19: Of this kind of fear is the fear of the judgment that is in the Shechinah, as is said in the Idra (Ha'azinu 292a), from the words of Rabbi Shimon: "all my days I was troubled that the world should not be burned in [God's] righteous judgments." One must fear lest he be the cause of the world's being burned through judgments - for perhaps the world is half meritorious and half guilty, and if, Heaven forfend, he tips the balance for the whole world to the side of guilt and causes, through him, a plague or famine to come upon the world - all those righteous people who die, he is the cause of their death, and all the poor who cry out and die of famine, he is the cause for them - and this is "woe to him," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:20: Therefore one must always avoid being idle from Torah or a commandment, as they said in the Talmud (Menachot 41a): "an angel found Rav Katina wrapped in a sheet [without tzitzit]," and so on. He said to him, do you punish for [neglecting] a positive commandment? He said to him, at a time when there is wrath [in the world], we do punish. We see, then, that they punish, at a time of wrath in the world, for neglecting a commandment; and engagement with Torah is [also] a positive commandment, and there is no doubt that they punish for that too - and it did not need to be mentioned [explicitly] because Rabbi Katina was not idle from Torah. Therefore one must be exceedingly careful and diligent in his work, the work of Heaven, so as not to be found idle and be punished - for at a time of wrath, the attribute of strict justice rules in its judgments, and one must be careful that the world not be burned in its judgments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:21: At all times a person is obligated to supply the oil of Torah and commandments to the lamp above his head, for "the LORD your God is a consuming fire," as is explained in Parashat Bereshit (Zohar 51a-b); how much more so, Heaven forfend, at a time of wrath, when great care and diligence are needed, since it is within his power to repair and draw forth a flow of mercy to turn the attribute of judgment into the attribute of mercy - while one who is lazy will be punished, Heaven forfend.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:22: We find that Rabbah, peace be upon him, used to call himself an intermediate person [beinoni]. They said in Berachot (61b): Rabbah said, one such as I am is an intermediate person. Abaye said to him: the Master leaves no life for any creature [if even you are only intermediate, who could be considered righteous]! And Rabbah said: a person knows within himself whether he is completely righteous or completely wicked. And Rabbah said: the world was created only for the completely righteous or the completely wicked. And Rabbah said: the whole world was created only for the sake of Ahab son of Omri and for the sake of Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa - for Ahab, this world; for Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa, the World to Come - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:23: Further, our Sages, of blessed memory, said in Midrash Vayikra Rabbah (4:2), on the verse (Ecclesiastes 6:7), "all the labor of man is for his mouth, and yet the soul is not satisfied" - in these words: "'and yet the soul is not satisfied' - because this soul knows that whatever it labors for is for itself, therefore it is never satisfied with commandments and good deeds. Rabbi Levi said: [it is like] a commoner who married a princess - even if he feeds her all the delicacies of the world, he has not fulfilled his obligation to her, because she is a princess. So too, whatever a person does for the soul, he has not fulfilled his obligation to it, because it is from above" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:24: Further, several things that arouse a person to be exacting in his deeds and careful of sin are explained in tractate Chagigah (4b), in these words: "when Rabbi Ami reached this verse, he wept (Lamentations 3:29), 'let him put his mouth in the dust, perhaps there is hope' - he said, all this, and [only] 'perhaps'? When Rabbi Ami reached this verse, he wept (Zephaniah 2:3), 'seek righteousness, seek humility; perhaps you will be hidden on the day of the LORD's anger' - he said, all this, and [only] 'perhaps'? When Rabbi Asi reached this verse, he wept (Amos 5:15), 'hate evil and love good, and establish justice in the gate; perhaps the LORD, God of Hosts, will be gracious' - he said, all this, and [only] 'perhaps'? When Rav Yosef reached this verse, he wept (Proverbs 13:23), 'and some are swept away without justice' - he said, is there a person who departs before his time? Yes, there is such a thing, and so on. When Rabbi Yochanan reached this verse, he wept (Job 2:3), 'and you incited Me against him, to destroy him without cause' - a servant whose master is incited against him has no remedy. When Rabbi Yochanan reached this verse, he wept (ibid. 15:15), 'behold, He puts no trust in His holy ones' - in whom, then, will He trust?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:25: Rabbi Yochanan, when he reached this verse, wept (Malachi 3:5), "and I will draw near to you for judgment, and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, and against the adulterers, and against those who swear falsely, and against those who oppress the hired worker's wages" - a servant against whom his master draws near to judge him, and hastens to testify against him, has no remedy. Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai said: woe to us, for Scripture has weighed light [sins] as heavy ones! [It weighs] light [sins] as heavy ones - Rashi explains: those who oppress the hired worker's wages are equated with adulterers and sorcerers.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:26: Rabbi Yochanan, when he reached this verse, wept (Ecclesiastes 12:14), "for God will bring every deed into judgment, concerning every hidden thing" - a servant whose master weighs unwitting acts as deliberate ones has no remedy. What is meant by "concerning every hidden thing"? Rav said, this refers to one who kills a louse in front of his fellow and is disgusted by it [an act so trivial it's normally unaccountable]; and Shmuel said, this refers to one who spits in front of his fellow and is disgusted by it. What is meant by "whether it is good or evil"? Rashi explains that this indicates that He brings even the good into judgment [scrutinizing even good deeds for impure motives]. The school of Rabbi Yannai say: this refers to one who gives charity to a poor person publicly. As when Rabbi Yannai saw a certain man giving a coin to a poor man publicly, he said to him: better that you had not given it to him at all than to give it to him now and shame him. The school of Rabbi Yannai say [further]: this refers to one who gives charity to a woman in private, which brings her under suspicion. Rava said, this refers to one who sends his wife meat that is not [properly] cut/checked - Rashi explains: not cleared of the forbidden fat and sinews, on Sabbath eves, since because they hurry to prepare for the Sabbath they do not pay attention to whether it has been checked. But did Rava himself send [meat that way]? [No,] the daughter of Rav Chisda [his wife] was different, for he was certain of her [reliability].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 6:27: Rabbi Yochanan, when he reached this verse, wept (Deuteronomy 31:21), "and it shall be, when many evils and troubles come upon them" - a servant for whom his master brings about evils and troubles has no remedy. And we further say there: Rabbi Ila was going up the stairway of the house of Rabbah bar Shila; he heard a child reciting (Amos 4:13), "for behold, He forms the mountains and creates the wind, and declares to man what is his thought [sicho]" - he said, a servant to whom his master declares his very thought has no remedy. What is meant by "his thought [sicho]"? Rav said: even the idle conversation between a man and his wife is declared to a person at the time of death - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:1: One must fear sin, for in many ways the sinner angers the Creator, blessed be He. The first is what Scripture says (Jeremiah 23:24), "can a man hide himself in secret places so that I do not see him? says the LORD; do I not fill the heaven and the earth? says the LORD." The explanation of this verse is given in Midrash Tanchuma (Naso 4-5): "'can a man hide himself in secret places...' - a parable of an architect who built a city and made tunnels within it," and so on. So the Holy One, blessed be He, says to adulterers: from Me you hide yourselves? As it is said (Job 24:15), "and the eye of the adulterer watches for twilight, saying, no eye will see me, and he puts a covering on his face." The adulterer says, no creature knows of me - but My eyes range through the whole earth! What is the way of transgressors? They watch for the hour of darkness, the hour of gloom - and so too thieves: "in the dark he breaks into houses" (ibid. 24:16); and so it says (Isaiah 29:15), "woe to those who go to great depths to hide their counsel from the LORD, and their deeds are in the dark, and they say, who sees us, and who knows us?" The adulterer is more severe, for he removes the Shechinah, as it were - He who fills the upper and lower worlds, as it is said (Jeremiah 23:24), "do I not fill the heaven and the earth?" And in what place is this man committing adultery? When he comes to commit adultery, he says to the Omnipresent, remove Yourself and give me a single hour - and, as it were, because He is slow to anger, He gives him room, as it is said (Job 11:11), "for He knows men of falsehood, and sees iniquity, though He does not appear to consider it." And it says, "and he puts a covering on his face" [they ask that she not conceive from him, but only that their desire be fulfilled, and they do not know that the Holy One, blessed be He, publicizes it in the world] - He who sits in the hidden supernal place arranges that the child conceived from him shall have a face resembling the adulterer's own" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:2: It is explained that there are two kinds of ugliness and disgrace in the sinner: the first is that he demeans the King by saying that He does not watch over him, since he hides himself - this is "can a man hide himself in secret places so that I do not see him? says the LORD" - and here the accent [pausal break] falls. "Do I not fill the heaven and the earth?" is the second blemish - that he removes the Shechinah, as it were, [when in truth] the Holy One, blessed be He, fills [everything], and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:3: Similarly, it is said in the Mishnah (Chagigah, chapter 2, mishnah 1): "whoever has no regard for the honor of his Maker, it would have been better for him not to have come into the world." It is explained in the Talmud (Chagigah 16a): Rav Yosef said, this refers to one who commits a transgression in secret - for Rabbi Yitzchak said, whoever commits a transgression in secret is as though he pushes against the feet of the Shechinah, as it is said (Isaiah 66:1), "the heavens are My throne, and the earth is My footstool" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:4: Similarly, it is said in Berachot, chapter Tefillat HaShachar (28b): when Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai fell ill, his disciples entered to visit him, and so on. They said to him, our teacher, bless us. He said to them, may it be [God's] will that the fear of Heaven be upon you like the fear of flesh and blood. They said to him, our teacher, [is that] all? He said to them, would that it were so! Know that when a person commits a transgression in secret, he says, may no person see me - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:5: Similar to the parable stated in this midrash on "can a man hide himself in secret places," and so on, Rashbi, of blessed memory, explained (Noach 68a): "Rabbi Chiya opened [with the verse] (Jeremiah 23:24), 'can a man hide himself in secret places so that I do not see him? says the LORD.' How many people are dulled of heart and closed of eye, who do not take heed and do not know the glory of their Master, of whom it is written, 'do I not fill the heaven and the earth?' How can they seek to hide from their sins and say, who sees us, who knows us - yet it is written, 'and their deeds are in the dark'? Where can they hide from Him? [It is like] a king who built a palace and made hidden tunnels beneath the earth. In time, the members of the king's palace rebelled; the king brought distress upon them with his armies. What did they do? They went and hid themselves in those hidden tunnel-openings. The king said: I am the one who made them, and I made light and darkness, and yet you seek to hide from before Me! This is [the meaning of] 'can a man hide himself in secret places so that I do not see him? says the LORD' - I am the One who made the hidden tunnels, and made darkness and light, and how could you hide from before Me? Come and see: when a person sins before his Master and prolongs his self-concealment, the Holy One, blessed be He, executes judgment upon him openly; but when a person purifies himself, the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to conceal him so that he not be seen 'on the day of the LORD's anger'" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:6: And in the Midrash Bamidbar Rabbah, section 9 (1), a similar parable is brought concerning the adulterer and adulteress, and they say in the application, in these words: "so said the Holy One, blessed be He, to adulterers: from Me you hide yourselves - but am I not the One who created the hearts? This is [the meaning of] (Jeremiah 17:10), 'I, the LORD, search the heart and test the innermost being,' and so on. Therefore it is said, 'and you forgot the God who formed you' - I created you, and made you full of tunnels - these being the hearts and the kidneys - and yet you forget Me and are false to Me, [saying] I do not see and do not know your deeds" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:7: Regarding the particulars of [divine] providence, Elihu said (Job 34:21-22), "for His eyes are on the ways of man, and He sees all his steps; there is no darkness, nor deep shadow, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:8: Further, he angers Him in a second manner: for His attribute, blessed be He, is to do good and show mercy, and they turn it from the attribute of mercy to the attribute of judgment - as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bereshit Rabbah 33:3), "cursed are the wicked, who turn the attribute of mercy into the attribute of judgment."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:9: As for what is written (Psalms 145:9), "and His mercies are over all His works" - our Sages, of blessed memory, explained in the Tanchuma (Yalkut Nachum, remez 561) that this refers to the righteous, in these words: on the verse (Nahum 1:7), "the LORD is good, a stronghold" - one might think for everyone; therefore Scripture teaches, "and He knows those who take refuge in Him." Similarly (Lamentations 3:25), "the LORD is good to those who wait for Him" - one might think for everyone; therefore Scripture teaches, "to the soul that seeks Him." Similarly (Psalms 145:9), "the LORD is good to all" - one might think for everyone; therefore Scripture teaches, "and His mercies are over all His works" - to the extent relevant here. And "His works" refers to the righteous, for they are deeds specifically His own, as in (Isaiah 60:21), "and your people, all of them righteous... the work of My hands, in which I glory." And so in the Zohar, Parashat Lech Lecha (82b), that the righteous are the fruit of the deeds of the Holy One, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:10: Further, it is said in the Tanchuma (Bechukotai 2), on the verse (Hosea 9:17), "my God will reject them, because they did not listen to Him, and they shall be wanderers among the nations," and so on: "the Holy One, blessed be He, said: I am called 'the LORD, a merciful and gracious God,' but because of your sins He has made Himself cruel, as it is said (Lamentations 2:5), 'the LORD has become like an enemy'" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:11: Of this kind is the matter that one who commits a single transgression acquires for himself a single accuser (Avot 4:11), and the accuser stands to accuse and arouse the [forces of] judgment until the portion of judgment is given to him to exact payment from the one who committed it - and this is (Job 34:11), "for the work of a man He will render to him," as is explained in the Zohar, Parashat Korach (177a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:12: Further, our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Shabbat 145b), on "your new moons and your appointed feasts My soul hates; they have become a burden to Me" (Isaiah 1:14) - what is meant by "they have become a burden to Me"? Rabbi Elazar said: the Holy One, blessed be He, said, it is not enough for the wicked that they sin, but they also burden Me to determine what harsh decree to bring upon them - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:13: Further, our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the Tanchuma, on the verse (Jeremiah 3:19), "and I said, how shall I place you among the children" - Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat said: what is meant by "eshitcha" [I shall place you]? It had arisen in My thought that only I and you would be in the world - why have you done this to Me, to bring the nations of the world in between us? And this expression [shata] means only separation, as it says (Genesis 30:40), "and he set [vayashet] his own flocks apart." Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said: there was great love between Me and you - why have you done this to Me, that I should hate you? And this expression means only hatred, as it is said (Genesis 3:15), "and I will put [ashit] enmity." Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: I plead in your defense - why have you done this to Me, that I should accuse you and find you liable? And this expression means only liability, as it is said (Exodus 21:30), "if a ransom is laid [yushat] upon him." Rabbi Berachiah said: you were as dear to Me as a person who has a single field, which he manures, hoes, and weeds - why have you done this to Me, to make yourselves ownerless? And this expression means only "ownerless" [hefker], as it is said (Isaiah 5:6), "and I will lay it waste [ashitehu]" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:14: Explained in this passage are four aspects of the love the Holy One, blessed be He, has for Israel, which, because of our sins, all turned to hatred; and one might relate them to the four letters of the Name, in their order, and each teacher who states one of them does not disagree with the others - and the discerning reader will understand the matter on his own. I shall hint a little to you: Rabbi Berachiah stated the last of them, which corresponds to the final Heh - "you were as dear to Me as a person who has a single field," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:15: Further, a third [reason]: the Holy One, blessed be He, is angry with the wicked person, and all of Israel is punished on his account; and so in Midrash Vayikra Rabbah (4:6), in these words: "'Israel is a scattered sheep' (Jeremiah 50:17) - Israel is compared to a sheep: just as it is the way of a sheep, when struck in one of its limbs, for all [its limbs] to feel it, so too when one Israelite sins, all are punished. It was taught by Rashbi: a parable of two men who were in a boat; one of them took a drill and began to drill beneath himself. His companions said to him, why are you doing this? He said to them, what does it matter to you? I am only drilling beneath myself! They said to him, because you are flooding the boat upon us! Job likewise said (Job 19:4), 'and even if indeed I have erred, my error remains with myself'; his companions said to him (ibid. 34:37), 'for he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps [his hands mockingly] among us' - you are bringing our iniquities upon us" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:16: Further, a fourth [reason]: the Holy One, blessed be He, is angry with the wicked person because He gave him a good way and an evil way, and he abandoned the good; and so it is said in the Midrash (Midrash Tehillim), on the verse (Psalms 36:5), "he plots iniquity upon his bed; he sets himself on a way that is not good" - in these words: "He gave them two ways, one evil and one good, and they abandon the good and walk in the evil; and so it says (Proverbs 2:13), 'who forsake the paths of uprightness... who rejoice in doing evil,' and so on - hence, 'he sets himself on a way that is not good'" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:17: Further, a fifth [reason]: the Holy One, blessed be He, is angry with the wicked person because of the harm he causes to himself and to his soul through the cause of his sin. Our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the Midrash (Midrash Tehillim), on the verse (Psalms 51:9), "purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean" - in these words: "from here [we learn] that whoever commits a transgression is as though he defiles himself with the impurity of a dead body [tumat nefesh], and is sprinkled upon only with hyssop, as it is said, 'purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean.' But was David [actually ritually] defiled? Rather, it is the sin that desecrated the soul - as it says (ibid. 109:22), 'and my heart is slain [profaned] within me'" - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:18: To understand this matter precisely - how a person blemishes his own soul so that we can say he has killed it and made it a corpse - we must know what is agreed upon in the Zohar (Mishpatim 94b) and in the Tikkunim (79a): that a person has "ruach" [spirit] and "nefesh" [soul] and "neshamah" [higher soul], and there is also "nefesh," "ruach," and "neshamah" corresponding to [the levels of] "chayah" and "yechidah" [or: "throne"], as is explained in the Tikkunim (79a), and likewise at the beginning of Parashat Mishpatim (94b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:19: One must know that just as the physical person has two hundred forty-eight physical limbs, so too the soul that is clothed in these two hundred forty-eight limbs has two hundred forty-eight spiritual limbs; and the soul is truly what is called "Adam," as I explained above - for what is said (Genesis 1:27), "and God created man [Adam] in His image," refers to the soul, for the body is called "the flesh of man [adam]," as it is said (Exodus 30:32), "upon the flesh of man it shall not be poured." And so Rashbi explained (Bereshit 20b), in these words: "the spirit, from the holy side, its body is a garment for it - Adam; and therefore it is written (Job 10:11), 'skin and flesh You have clothed me,' and so on - the flesh of Adam is their garment, and everywhere it is written 'flesh of Adam' [it means]: Adam within, flesh the garment of Adam" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 7:20: And because the soul comprises two hundred forty-eight spiritual limbs, it acts and clothes itself in that drop [of seed] to fashion a vessel for its work; and thus the body is found to be the mold of the soul. For this reason the forms of people differ by the thousands and myriads, according to the quarry of their soul, as is explained in the Tikkunim (128a-b).
